guides.title: Gifts for kids, recall-aware, 2026
guides.label: Kids
guides.description: Mainstream kids product lines, with the official CPSC or Health Canada check to do before you buy.

faqs.a: Six mainstream kids product lines sold in US and Canada stores. Each line says why it is listed and which official page to use for the check. The button opens an Amazon search for those words. It is not a product page.

faqs.q: Where do I search a toy recall?
faqs.a: Search the brand and the set or model number on CPSC Recalls for a US purchase and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts for a Canadian purchase. Match the number on the box to the number on the notice.

faqs.q: Does this list replace the toy safety guides?
faqs.a: No. Toy safety covers button and coin batteries, magnets, water beads, and ride-ons and scooters. This page links those guides. A line here is not a catalogue card.

picks.name: LEGO Duplo brick set
picks.why: On this list because LEGO Duplo is a mainstream brick set for younger children.

check.text: Read the age range on the box.
Health Canada toy safety tips

say a toy that is safe for an older child may be dangerous for a younger one, and say not to give building sets for older children to children under 3. The same page says a toy or a removable part that fits inside a toilet paper roll is too small for safe play for children under 3.
CPSC small-parts guidance

says products intended for children under 3 that present a choking, aspiration, or ingestion hazard because of small parts are banned under 16 CFR part 1501. Search the set number on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Crayola crayons
picks.why: On this list because Crayola crayons are a mainstream kids art supply.

check.text: Read the age label and any warning.
Health Canada’s back-to-school page

says to buy art supplies labeled for children’s use and to avoid products with hazard symbols. It says a label that cites ASTM D 4236 means a medical professional reviewed the product and the label lists hazards and safe-use instructions. It says that citation does not mean the product is non-toxic.
CPSC small-parts guidance
lists writing materials such as crayons among the products excluded from the small-parts ban. Search the brand on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Hot Wheels toy cars
picks.why: On this list because Hot Wheels is a mainstream toy-car line.

check.text: Read the age label.
Health Canada’s toy-type page
lists wheels and tires from small toy cars among the small parts not to give to young children.
CPSC small-parts guidance

says a product intended for children under 3 is banned if the toy, a separate part, or a piece that breaks off during CPSC use-and-abuse testing fits entirely in the small parts cylinder. Search the assortment number on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Radio Flyer wagon
picks.why: On this list because a Radio Flyer wagon is a mainstream ride-on toy.

check.text: Read the age, size, and weight lines on the box.
Health Canada’s ride-on advice

says falls are the most common injuries with ride-on toys, tricycles, scooters, and wagons. It says to match the toy to the child’s age, size, and abilities, to keep riding on flat traffic-free paths, and not to allow standing or kneeling in a wagon. It says roads, driveways, stairs, and pools are not places to ride. More ride-on checks are on the
ride-ons and scooters guide
. Search the model number on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Razor kick scooter
picks.why: On this list because a Razor kick scooter is a mainstream kids scooter. The search words are for a kick scooter.

check.text: Read whether the listing has a battery. If it does, use the
ride-ons and scooters guide
for the UL 2272 check.
Health Canada’s ride-on advice
says to use helmets especially for scooters.
Health Canada’s back-to-school page
lists a bicycle helmet for electric and non-electric scooters and says to look for a certification label such as CSA, ASTM, EN, or SNELL.
CPSC bicycle-helmet guidance
says US bicycle helmets are covered by 16 CFR part 1203. Search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Magna-Tiles building set
picks.why: On this list because Magna-Tiles is a mainstream magnetic building set.

check.text: Read the age label and look at the size of the pieces.
Health Canada’s magnetic-toy advice
says construction sets can contain magnets, and says to buy magnetic toys whose pieces are too big to swallow. The
magnets guide

quotes the CPSC rule for novelty magnet sets and the Health Canada assessment under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act. CPSC says that rule does not apply to toys for children under 14, because 16 CFR part 1250 already covers those toys. Search the set number on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

faqs.q: Where do I search one of these for a recall?
faqs.a: Search the brand and the model number on CPSC Recalls for a US purchase and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts for a Canadian purchase. Match the number on the unit to the number on the notice.

faqs.q: Does this list replace the Thanksgiving guides?
faqs.a: No. Thanksgiving covers turkey fryers, pressure cookers, turkey temperatures, and kitchen fires. This page links those guides. A line here is not a catalogue card. A catalogue card for one Dutch oven or one knife does not cover a different model.

picks.name: ThermoWorks Thermapen
picks.why: On this list because a ThermoWorks Thermapen is a widely sold instant-read food thermometer, and USDA FSIS says to check a turkey with a food thermometer.

check.text: Read the model on the thermometer.
USDA Turkey Basics: Safe Cooking
says to use a food thermometer and to reach 165 °F in the innermost part of the thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast.
Let’s Talk Turkey
says a pop-up indicator is still checked with a food thermometer in those places. The
September 3, 2014 CPSC probe notice
names iDevices Pro probes made from May 2014 through June 2014, not every thermometer. More is on the
turkey temperatures guide
. Search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Roasting pan with a wire rack
picks.why: On this list because USDA FSIS says to set a turkey breast-side up on a flat wire rack in a shallow roasting pan.

check.text: Read the material and the depth on the pan.
USDA Turkey Basics: Safe Cooking

says to use a shallow roasting pan 2 to 2 1/2 inches deep, and says a dark roasting pan cooks faster than a shiny one. It still says doneness is 165 °F on a food thermometer. Search the brand and model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Wusthof carving set
picks.why: On this list because USDA FSIS says to let the turkey stand 20 minutes before carving, and a carving set is sold for that step.

check.text: Read the model on the knife or the box.
USDA Turkey Basics: Safe Cooking
says the 20-minute stand is so the juices set and the turkey carves more easily. The catalogue card for the
Wusthof Classic 8-inch cook’s knife
is a different product from a carving set. Search the carving-set model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Le Creuset Dutch oven
picks.why: On this list because a Le Creuset Dutch oven is a widely sold lidded pot, and the CPSC holiday cooking release says to smother a grease fire by sliding a lid over the pan.

check.text: Read the size on the pot. The November 19, 2025
CPSC holiday cooking release
says to slide a lid over a grease fire and turn off the burner, and never to use water. The
NFPA desk reference
says not to move the pan and to leave the lid on until the pan has cooled. The catalogue card for the
Le Creuset Signature 5.5-quart Dutch oven
is one model. A clear line on that card does not cover a different size. Search the size you are buying on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: OXO gravy separator
picks.why: On this list because an OXO gravy separator is a widely sold tool for separating fat from pan drippings, and USDA FSIS gives a storage time for gravy.

check.text: Read the model on the separator.
Let’s Talk Turkey

says to discard gravy left out longer than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 °F, and to use refrigerated gravy within 3 to 4 days. It says reheated turkey should reach 165 °F. Search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.

picks.name: Kidde kitchen fire extinguisher
picks.why: On this list because a Kidde fire extinguisher is a widely sold home extinguisher, and the CPSC holiday cooking release says to have a fire extinguisher nearby and know how to use it.

check.text: Read the model number, the date code, and the classification label.
USFA’s extinguisher page

says to look for a UL Listed or ULC Listed label, describes Class B for grease and other flammable liquids, Class K for cooking oils and fats, and multipurpose A-B-C extinguishers for most home fires. The November 2, 2017
CPSC Kidde notice
names plastic-handle models made from January 1, 1973 through August 15, 2017, and push-button Pindicator extinguishers. It counts units sold in Canada. More is on the
kitchen fires guide
. Search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts.
